I am 47 and have farmed this 10.9 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, but I know this land by touch and by season. My household has four people, and some of us work off-farm in town, so I cannot handle too much labor-intensive crop. I have a well, so when the rain does not come I can pump water.

The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I will keep about 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what feeds the family—winter wheat through to June, then summer maize planted straight after harvest. There is only about a week between wheat harvest and maize sowing, so I will not plough that land; I will direct-seed the maize to catch the summer season. On the remaining 2.9 mu I will plant cotton in late April. Cotton is more work and needs more pesticide, but it brings cash for daily expenses and school costs. For the wheat I will top-dress urea at green-up and irrigate three times—green-up, jointing, and grain filling. For maize I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the jointing stage, irrigating twice when the summer drought hits. Cotton needs more potassium and more sprays for bollworm, and I will irrigate it three times. I use improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, and improved cotton seed. I rotary till before wheat and cotton planting, but the maize goes in with no-tillage because time is short after wheat harvest.
